日本語 Open the map

Will IntMap work here? Check it on the spot.

Open this page on a device your students or staff will use, on the same network, and run the check. It tests what the map needs from the browser and asks each of the 113 outside services IntMap loads, then tells you what works, what is blocked and what to allow.

See the list to allow

The check sends one request from this device to each service listed below — the same requests the map makes when it is used. Nothing is sent to IntMap. It takes a few seconds, and at most 160 seconds on a network that drops requests without answering.

Result

      Ask us, with the report attached

      Services to allow

      Give this list to whoever manages the network filter. Each service is listed with what it is used for; the privacy policy and the security page say what each one is sent. Privacy → Security →

      What this check cannot tell you

      • A filter that shows its own page in place of a blocked service looks «reached» here: a web page is not allowed to read another site's answer. If parts of the map are still missing after the check passes, look for such a block page in the filter's log.
      • It describes one device on one network at one moment. Another room, another network or another time of day can differ.
      • Services chosen while the map is in use — a webcam's own server, the site of a news article, a map server address a reader types in — are not in this list.
      • «Answered last night» is IntMap's own nightly check of the same services, run from a server outside your network.
